text:
Diagnosed with ADD as a child via. A 6 week double blind study with teachers, parents, doctor. I still take medication as an adult and makes me able to be a software engineer. Without it, I do maybe 4 hour work days. Unsustainable.

My largest challenge is dealing with misinformation and the, "oh everyone has ADHD" perception. It's painful to feel so dismissed when my disorder drastically affects who I am, and diagnosis and treatment affects who I get to be.

I just can't justify writing my team's code base in typescript. I don't want to make that move, setting us down a very specific path. I don't want to add another layer of training to develop on our codebase, but mainly, I just don't have the confidence that it's a right or wrong choice, and its a big choice.

But I get a sense that it would be great to try for smaller, disposable projects as that's limited risk.

Does anyone else struggle with TypeScript simply because of how big a choice it can be?

I hear you. I'm terrified by the kinds of interviews that want programming trivia. In the last three years I've never had to code a binary search tree. But I should be able to show you I'm very comfortable with Python.

I find it beautiful that some things in math are so easily and convincingly disprovable that brute force is a valid approach.

Once you have the numbers, it's easily reproducible.
Things that look like colonialism are no longer considered acceptable in this era.
